pictures.scene: Brueghel, Christ on the Sea of Galilee — a small fishing boat driven over a heaving green sea under a stormy sky, banks of dark green-black cloud piled right across it with the sun breaking through in a patch of yellow at the top right, a jagged rock island and other sails far off on the water, the boat's brown sail flogging loose and a man climbing the mast to haul it in, the disciples crowded together in the hull in red, pink, yellow, blue and white, one at the bow throwing his head back and crying out, an old white-bearded man leaning forward with his arm flung out, another slumped over the gunwale, a man at the oar in a white shirt, Jesus lying back asleep in the stern in a blue robe and a rose mantle with his head resting on his hand, and the broken water running white along the side of the boat, after this, jesus traveled throughout galilee, …
pictures.name: pd_brueghel_galilea

pictures.scene: Cornelius, Joseph Recognised by His Brothers — a fresco in pale clear colour set in an open arcade whose round arches give on a blue sky, a square tower, dark trees and a colonnaded court beyond, Joseph standing huge in the foreground in a long white mantle over a green sleeved tunic with a rose cloth wound about his red cap, bending right down to take his youngest brother's head in both hands and press his cheek against it with his eyes closed, the boy in a dull red robe reaching up to him, a brother kneeling in the near corner in a pale blue robe with his back turned and his head bowed and staffs lying across the floor beside him, a knot of bearded brothers crowding in at the right in brown and yellow with their caps pushed back and their faces all turned toward him, a dark-haired man standing at the left edge, and a pale pink marble floor and a low step running across the bottom, for even his own brothers did not believe in him, …
pictures.name: pd_cornelius_broeders

pictures.scene: Breu, The Crowd Cries Out Against Him — a press of accusers crowded right up to the front of the picture, a high priest at the left in a jewelled white and gold mitre and a pale yellow cope fringed with gold over a green robe and a figured red mantle, his eyes lowered and both hands raised as he counts off his charges, a man standing in front of him in a scarlet gown with a white fur hood, a black cap and black and gold embroidered sleeves, his head thrown back and his mouth open in a shout with a rolled paper gripped in his hand, a second mitred head pushing in at the right with a black-bearded man staring up beside him, and behind them a bank of shouting faces in red and green turbans and black caps with their mouths open and their hands flung up past the top of the picture, pale stone steps cutting across the lower left corner, it hates me, because i testify that its works are evil, …
pictures.name: pd_breu_de_menigte_roept_tegen_hem

pictures.scene: Bauernfeind, Jerusalem from the Mount of Olives — the whole city spread out in pale gold morning light below a soft green and cream sky banded with a long streak of lilac haze, the domes, towers and flat roofs of the old town crowded together behind the long tan city wall, the great blue-tiled dome of the Haram rising at the right above its arcaded platform and a second low dome at the left among dark cypresses and olive trees, the bare brown valley sweeping down in front of the wall with scattered olives and a stony track winding through it, and at the bottom of the picture a party of pilgrims coming up the road, an old white-bearded man in a grey coat leaning on his staff with his hat in his hand, a woman in a red skirt and a yellow headcloth carrying a shallow basket of fruit on her head, men in long black coats and dark caps walking close together behind them, and rough field walls of piled stones along the path, go up to the feast on your own, i am not going up to this feast, …
pictures.name: pd_bauernfeind_jerusalem_from_the_mount_of_olives

pictures.scene: Elsheimer, The Flight into Egypt — a journey made by night under a deep blue sky thick with stars, the Milky Way drifting across it in a pale band and long low clouds lying near the horizon, a full moon standing low at the right and laying a broad silver track down a still pool that runs back into the dark, great black masses of oak and willow filling the middle of the picture with one bare tree silhouetted against the moonlight, and at the lower left the little family moving quietly along the water's edge, Mary wrapped in a blue-green mantle and a white headcloth riding the donkey with the Child held close against her shoulder and his small face turned out toward us, Joseph walking beside her in a red tunic with his sleeves pushed back, barefoot, his grey-bearded face lit from below by the burning torch he carries low in his hand, a bundle and a water flask strapped to the saddle behind them, and nothing stirring anywhere else in the whole night, but after his brothers had gone up to the feast, he also went, not publicly, but in secret, …
pictures.name: pd_elsheimer_the_flight_into_egypt

pictures.scene: Beuckelaer, The Vegetable Market — a market stall under a rough timbered shelter with leafy trees and a glimpse of a green path and a far-off tower showing through the posts behind, the boards heaped so full that the produce fills most of the picture, a wide basket of pears, apples, pomegranates and dark red plums piled at the upper left with walnuts spilling below it, melons, pumpkins, cauliflowers, artichokes, cucumbers, asparagus and great pale cabbages banked along the bottom, a round basket of cherries and currants in the middle and another of white curled endive, a young market woman sitting among it all in a white chemise with the sleeves rolled above her elbows, a rust-red bodice and a blue-grey apron, her reddish hair drawn back and her face turned straight out at us with a steady unsmiling look, one hand resting on the rim of the little red basket and the other on the handle of the big one, and an older woman in a straw hat and a green sleeve leaning in close behind her shoulder at the right edge, many in the crowds were whispering about him, …
pictures.name: pd_beuckelaer_groentemarkt

pictures.scene: Durer, Christ among the Doctors — a close press of heads and hands against a near-black ground, the boy at the centre in a blue-green robe with long waving red-gold hair and a fine rayed halo scratched in gold behind it, his young face lowered and calm, his two hands held up in front of him counting off a point on his fingers, an old teacher crowding in at the right with a gaunt wrinkled face, a hooked nose and an open mouth showing broken teeth, leaning in to argue and reaching both long bony hands toward the boy's, a second old man in a dark red mantle pushing in at the top left with a book held open at his chest, a white-bearded head at the lower right and another hand at the left edge holding a heavy clasped volume, a thick book with brass bosses raised in front of the boy and loose dog-eared leaves of another fanned open behind it, and nothing in the picture but faces, hands and books, how did this man attain such learning without having studied, …
pictures.name: pd_durer_doctors

pictures.scene: Bruegel, The Sermon of Saint John the Baptist — a preaching in the open air under great dark trees, hundreds of people packed together on the slope with every face turned one way, the preacher standing small in the middle distance in a plain brown robe with his hands put out as he speaks, a few listeners pressed close around him in red, green and grey, boys who have climbed the trunks and are hanging out along the branches to see over the heads, and in the near foreground a bank of broad backs and shoulders seen from behind, a man in a pale yellow mantle, another in a deep red cloak, a woman in a huge yellow cloak banded with red sitting on the ground with a small child at her shoulder, white linen headcloths, broad straw hats and black caps everywhere between, one lean man in a dark coat and red hose sprawled on the earth at the bottom left with a staff across his knees, and a single burgher's face in a black cap and a white ruff turned round to look straight out of the picture, my teaching is not my own, it comes from him who sent me, …
pictures.name: pd_bruegel_prediking

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, Moses Smashing the Tablets of the Law — one huge figure filling almost the whole picture against a bare tawny mountainside, an old man in a loose cream robe with wide sleeves pushed back over his forearms and a dark red sash at his waist, a gold band clasped on one wrist, his grey-brown hair standing out wild about his head and a long heavy beard falling over his chest, his face lit from the side and turned down toward us with the brows drawn and the eyes full of grief rather than anger, and both arms raised high over his head gripping the two dark stone tablets by their lower corners, the writing cut into them in rows of Hebrew letters that catch the light in gold, the tablets held up at the very top of the picture at the moment before he hurls them down, has not moses given you the law, yet not one of you keeps it, …
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_moses_smashing_the_tablets_of_the_law

pictures.scene: Metsu, The Sick Child — a quiet room with a pale grey plaster wall behind, a rolled map hanging from a rod at the left and a dark framed painting high at the right, a woman sitting with a sick little girl laid across her lap, the woman in a brown bodice with a wide white collar, a black cap edged with pearls over her dark hair and a pearl drop at her ear, a blue skirt over a red underskirt falling in heavy folds to the floor, her head bent right down and her face full of worry as she looks at the child, one hand holding the little arm and the other arm round the child's back to hold her up, the girl limp and heavy in a mustard yellow jacket and a white linen cap with her bare legs hanging down over her mother's knee and her white shift fallen across them, her small face pale and her eyes turned out at us without strength, i did one miracle, and you are all amazed, …
pictures.name: pd_metsu_the_sick_child

pictures.scene: Hirszenberg, Sabbath Rest — a plain olive-green room on the day of rest, a tall window at the left hung with a looped white lace curtain and the pale winter light of the town coming through the small panes, a many-branched brass sabbath lamp hanging from the ceiling and a framed picture on the far wall, a young man sitting on a low chair in a dark coat and a blue cloth cap holding a small book open in both hands and reading it with his head bent and his lips parted, a young woman standing behind him at the window in a coral-pink shawl drawn across her shoulders with her eyes lowered, an old grey-bearded man sunk down asleep in the near corner in a heavy brown coat with a second sleeper's head fallen across his knee, a woman in a grey shawl sitting with her back to us at the right with her face turned away in profile and another half-seen beside her, and the bare wooden floor and the dark press filling the lower corner, why are you angry with me for making the whole man well on the sabbath, …
pictures.name: pd_hirszenberg_sabbath_rest

pictures.scene: Millais, The Blind Girl — two girls resting at the edge of a wide common after rain, the whole meadow burning acid green in the sun with cattle, sheep and white horses grazing across it and a double rainbow standing out against a dark blue-grey storm sky above a village of red roofs, a church tower and tall elms, the elder girl sitting in front in a brown cloak drawn over her head and a worn golden skirt, her red hair loose, her face lifted and her eyes closed because she cannot see any of it, a little concertina resting on her lap with a card at her throat that reads pity the blind, a tortoiseshell butterfly settled on her shawl without her knowing, her younger sister pressed in against her shoulder in a dark green jacket and a blue skirt, her fair hair falling forward as she twists round and holds a fold of the cloak up to shade her eyes and stare at the rainbow, their two hands locked together between them, and the wet grass, rushes and a muddy pool worked out in detail all round them, stop judging by outward appearances, and start judging justly, …
pictures.name: pd_millais_the_blind_girl

pictures.scene: Springer, The Cathedral Square — a great gothic church rising over a town square in warm afternoon light under a worked sky of grey and cream cloud, the long flank of the nave carved with gables, buttresses and a huge wheel window, a tall open stonework spire climbing behind it and a second massive unfinished tower standing square and dark at the right, three deep arched doorways lined with rows of little stone saints at the foot of the front, old timbered and plastered houses crowding right up against the church on the left with their shutters and chimneys, a tree and low roofs at the right, and the cobbled square below full of ordinary business, a carter in a black hat leading a pale horse and a loaded cart, women in white caps and red and blue skirts standing talking in twos and threes, a boy carrying a basket on his back, a knot of men in dark coats sitting along a low parapet at the right, a few figures going up the steps into the doorway, and long shadows thrown across the stones, but we know where this man is from, …
pictures.name: pd_springer_kathedraal_plein

pictures.scene: de Wet, Christ Blessing the Children — a dim hall of heavy stone piers with a dark archway behind, Jesus seated on a low step at the centre in a cream robe and a dull red mantle with a soft ring of golden light about his bowed head, his hand laid against his breast and his face turned down toward the children at his knee, a young mother kneeling at the left in a white chemise, a blue skirt and an orange sash with a small child gathered against her arm and another infant held behind her, a little boy in grey kneeling with his hands put together and his face lifted, a girl in a cream gown and a striped cap kneeling square in the middle of the picture with her hands joined in prayer, a fair-haired child in blue leaning in close at his other side, a toddler being led forward at the right, a small boy in a red cap crawling across the bare floor at the bottom, an old white-bearded man standing watching from the shadow at the back and other heads crowding in at both edges, you know me, and you know where i am from, …
pictures.name: pd_dewet_christus_zegent_kinderen

pictures.scene: Aertsen, The Entry into Jerusalem — a procession coming down a stony track between rocky banks and thin windblown trees under a pale sky, Jesus riding in the middle of the picture on a donkey covered with a yellow cloth patterned in red and green, his hair falling loose over a grey-green tunic and a great crimson mantle gathered across his knees, one hand raised with two fingers lifted in blessing and his face quiet and turned slightly down, a dark-haired disciple in blue and a bald grey-bearded one walking close at the donkey's head, another pressing a hand to his face at the left edge, two men at the right in scarlet and olive bending right down to spread their cloaks across the road in front of the hooves, a red cloak and a yellow one already lying in the dirt, a second donkey's head showing behind, and all along the hillside behind them people coming on in knots and files, women with children, a man carrying a bundle, figures still winding over the ridge, but no one laid a hand on him, because his hour had not yet come, …
pictures.name: pd_aertsen_entry_jerusalem

pictures.scene: de Keyser, Officers of the Civic Guard — three armed officers standing full length and shoulder to shoulder against a dim brown wall with a pale blue and white banner furled on its pole behind them, the first in a plain brown doublet and breeches with a wide stiff white ruff and a broad black hat, a folded paper of orders held down at his side and his other hand opened toward us as he speaks, the second in a buff leather jerkin and a pale broad-brimmed hat with a deep lace collar and a sword and powder flask at his belt, both gloved hands closed over a long staff set upright on the floor, the third in a grey doublet worked with silver and an engraved steel shoulder plate, a yellow silk sash across his chest, a stiff lace ruff at his throat, a rapier with a basket hilt at his hip and a heavy black hat on his red hair, all three looking straight out at us, pikes and musket rests crossing behind them and a flagstone floor underfoot, they and the chief priests sent officers to arrest him, …
pictures.name: pd_de_keyser_schutters_wijk_iii

pictures.scene: Corot, The Road to Sevres — a chalky country road running away from us over the brow of a hill under a wide sky of soft blue and drifting white cloud, a great dark green tree standing full height along the whole right edge with its branches hanging out over the road and a thick bank of bushes and young trees below it, a slender silvery tree at the left above a low wall and a pale farmhouse half hidden in the green, the far country opening out in the middle distance in hazy blue and gold with the roofs and a far-off dome of a town just showing on the horizon, and one small lone figure walking away up the road with her back to us, a dark skirt and shawl, a white cap, and a bundle carried on her hip, already small against the distance and about to go over the rise, you will look for me, but you will not find me, …
pictures.name: pd_corot_road

pictures.scene: Tintoretto, Moses Striking the Rock — water breaking out of the dry rock for a thirsty people, a pale clouded sky across the top with dark feathery tree branches hanging in at both upper corners and a bare olive-grey hill behind, Moses standing full height in the middle of the picture in a deep crimson robe with a grey-green mantle slung across his shoulder, his white beard falling on his chest, a faint ring of light about his bald head and his face turned down toward the water, both arms flung wide, one hand still pointing back along the staff he has struck with, a great crowd of the people banked up behind him in rows of small lit faces under white headcloths, men and women pressed shoulder to shoulder right across the picture, a young woman kneeling at his feet in a golden orange gown and a rose and white bodice with her hair braided up, leaning out over the water with a vessel held ready and her face lifted, a bare arm reaching in from the right edge holding out a white bowl to be filled, another hand at the left steadying a wooden trough, and the new stream running out dark and foaming along the whole bottom of the picture, if anyone is thirsty, let him come to me and drink, …
pictures.name: pd_tintoretto_moses_striking_the_rock

pictures.scene: van Everdingen, The Waterfall — a northern torrent coming down through rocks in broad sheets of white water, the whole lower half of the picture filled with foam breaking over black boulders and a loose beam of timber tumbling in the race, smooth green glassy water sliding over the lip of the fall above it and running away to the left in a second channel, bare brown rock shelves and dark cliffs crowding in on both sides, a rough wooden footbridge of rails and planks built out over the rocks at the left with one small figure standing on it watching the water, a low turf-roofed log hut at the far left among the trees, a timber mill of grey boards and a broken shingled roof perched over the stream at the right with two tiny figures standing by the sluice above it, dark firs and autumn-brown oaks banked along the skyline and a steep wooden church tower with a slender spire rising behind them, and a sky of heavy grey and white cloud with a little clear blue showing through at the top left, streams of living water will flow from within him, …
pictures.name: pd_everdingen_bron

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, Portrait of an Old Woman — a very old woman seen close against a dim brown ground, her face taking almost all the light in the picture, the skin loose and deeply lined, the cheeks hollowed, the mouth a little open as though she had just spoken, and the dark eyes looking away past us with a long patient steadiness, a soft white linen cloth drawn close round her head and under her chin and a wide fur-lined hood of deep red and gold brocade laid over it and falling down both sides of her shoulders, a stiff pleated white ruff standing up at her throat, a black gown with a heavy chased silver clasp at the breast, a dark fur-edged cloak hung with tasselled silver cords over her arms, and both her old hands brought together low in front of her, the knuckles swollen, the veins standing out, holding a folded red cloth and resting one over the other, this is truly the prophet, …
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_prophetess_anna

pictures.scene: Botticelli, The Mystic Nativity — the sky over the stable at Bethlehem opened into burnished gold, a ring of angels joining hands and dancing round in it high above the roof, their gowns of rose, white, olive and dull gold swinging out behind them, each one carrying an olive branch with a long white scroll twisting round it and a little gold crown hung from the bough on a thread, one angel in deep green robes sinking down through the blue air in the middle of the picture with her eyes closed and her bare feet pointing down, a wreath of dark olive pressed into her hair, a bank of small dark firs and feathery olive trees along the hillside below, and on the thatched golden roof of the stable itself three angels kneeling close together, one in white, one in rose, one in green, with coloured wings and olive garlands in their loose hair, bending their heads over an open book held between them and one reaching across to touch the hand of another, from bethlehem, the village where david lived, …
pictures.name: pd_botticelli_mystic_nativity

pictures.scene: Coello, The Adoration of the Sacred Form — a great company of churchmen and officers packed into a candlelit sacristy, a long row of tall lit tapers burning across the top of the picture against the dark, a carved gilt reliquary house and a tall silver processional cross rising behind, a heavy gold-fronted altar table at the left spread with a damask cloth worked in yellow and gold, a rank of shaven-headed monks and canons crowded along the back in black habits with their heads turned together in talk, one of them holding up an open paper and another a rolled staff, a boy in a white surplice among them with his face lifted and his mouth open, a long-haired man in black kneeling in the middle of the picture in profile with a broad gold-embroidered sash across his shoulder, a lace cravat at his throat and a lit candle held upright in his gloved hand, and behind and beside him a close press of courtiers in dark coats, long curled wigs, lace cuffs and red ribbons, some holding candles of their own and all of them looking one way, then the officers returned to the chief priests and pharisees, …
pictures.name: pd_coello_vergadering

pictures.scene: Raphael, Saint Paul Preaching at Athens — a man preaching in the open on a flight of pale stone steps between tall grey buildings, a deep arch and heavy cornices behind him at the left, a bank of fluted columns and a round pillared temple at the right with a glimpse of towers and a distant town beyond, Paul standing full height at the left of the picture in a coral-rose mantle wrapped round a sea-green tunic, barefoot on the step, his dark curling hair and beard and a faint ring of light at his head, his face turned in profile as he speaks and both arms thrown up with the hands open wide above him, a young man in green sitting at his feet with his curling hair and his round face lifted straight up at the preacher and one hand put out, a row of listeners seated close together on the step beyond him in olive, ochre, deep red and rose, some leaning forward with their chins in their hands, one white-bearded old man with his arms folded, two more standing behind with a hand pressed to the mouth, every one of them held still and watching him, and two small figures talking at the foot of a column in the sunlit square behind, never has anyone spoken like this man, …
pictures.name: pd_raphael_prediking

pictures.scene: Hart, The Feast of the Rejoicing of the Law — the scrolls of the law carried round a synagogue on the day of rejoicing, a vaulted hall of pale stone arches with two heavy silver lamps hanging down on long chains and a white carved and gilded reading platform standing in the middle, a branched candlestick and tall candles burning on it, a railed gallery behind hung with an embroidered cloth worked in flowers where old men in prayer shawls and bright turbans stand with two boys leaning on the rail between them, and in front, coming forward across the tiled floor, a procession of men carrying the scrolls in their arms, a bearded man in a broad black hat and a wide striped prayer shawl holding one dressed in a scarlet and gold mantle with silver finials and a silver pointer hanging from it, another close behind him in a long grey coat with a second scroll in blue velvet and a silver crown, more faces and red caps crowding in at the left edge, and an old man in a crimson robe standing at the right by a dark carved desk with a book held against him, but this crowd that does not know the law, …
pictures.name: pd_hart_rejoicing_of_the_law

pictures.scene: Delaroche, Joan of Arc Questioned in Prison — a prisoner being examined in a dark cell with bare stone walls and a shadowed vault above, a cardinal sitting at the left in a scarlet robe and mozzetta that fill nearly half the picture, a scarlet biretta on his head, a gold cross hanging on a chain at his breast and a white sleeve showing at his wrist, his old sunken face turned sharply round over his shoulder with the mouth drawn tight and the eyes narrowed, one hand gripping the arm of his chair and the other laid flat on his knee, a clerk half seen in the shadow at the far left edge with a pen and a sheet of paper held up, and at the right the young prisoner sitting up on a pallet of loose straw in a plain white shift with dark sleeves, a heavy iron ring and chain locked on her wrist and running down across the bed, her dark hair loose on her shoulders, her hands clasped tight together in front of her and her face lifted away from him toward the light, does our law convict a man without first hearing from him, …
pictures.name: pd_delaroche_verhoor

pictures.scene: Mauve, The Return of the Flock — a great flock of sheep coming home over the heath at the end of the day, a pale flat grey and cream sky across the top with three small birds crossing it and a low brown ridge shutting off the distance, the shepherd standing small and dark on the ridge in a heavy coat and a cap with his staff held out across the flock and his back to us, and below him the sheep filling almost the whole picture, scores of them packed close and moving straight toward us, their backs a mass of dirty cream and soft brown wool, heads down in the heather, a dark donkey walking among them at the right with a load on its back, one small white lamb standing alone and clear in the middle of the picture with its ears up, and the rough brown heath worked out below in tufts of ling, bare sand and dry grass trodden by the whole crowd of them, then each went to his own home, …
pictures.name: pd_mauve_the_return_of_the_flock

lines.text: After this, Jesus traveled throughout Galilee. He did not want to travel in Judea, because the Jews there were trying to kill Him. However, the Jewish Feast of Tabernacles was near.
So Jesus' brothers said to Him, Leave here and go to Judea, so that Your disciples there may see the works You are doing.
For no one who wants to be known publicly acts in secret. Since You are doing these things, show Yourself to the world.
For even His own brothers did not believe in Him.
Therefore Jesus told them, Although your time is always at hand, My time has not yet come.
The world cannot hate you, but it hates Me, because I testify that its works are evil.
Go up to the feast on your own. I am not going up to this feast, because My time has not yet come.
Having said this, Jesus remained in Galilee.
But after His brothers had gone up to the feast, He also went, not publicly, but in secret.
So the Jews were looking for Him at the feast and asking, Where is He?
Many in the crowds were whispering about Him. Some said, He is a good man. But others replied, No, He deceives the people.
Yet no one would speak publicly about Him for fear of the Jews.
About halfway through the feast, Jesus went up to the temple courts and began to teach.
The Jews were amazed and asked, How did this man attain such learning without having studied?
My teaching is not My own, Jesus replied. It comes from Him who sent Me.
If anyone desires to do His will, he will know whether My teaching is from God or whether I speak on My own.
He who speaks on his own authority seeks his own glory, but He who seeks the glory of the One who sent Him is a man of truth; in Him there is no falsehood.
Has not Moses given you the law? Yet not one of you keeps it. Why are you trying to kill Me?
You have a demon, the crowd replied. Who is trying to kill You?
Jesus answered them, I did one miracle, and you are all amazed.
But because Moses gave you circumcision, you circumcise a boy on the Sabbath, not that it is from Moses, but from the patriarchs.
If a boy can be circumcised on the Sabbath so that the law of Moses will not be broken, why are you angry with Me for making the whole man well on the Sabbath?
Stop judging by outward appearances, and start judging justly.
Then some of the people of Jerusalem began to say, Isn't this the man they are trying to kill?
Yet here He is, speaking publicly, and they are not saying anything to Him. Have the rulers truly recognized that this is the Christ?
But we know where this man is from. When the Christ comes, no one will know where He is from.
Then Jesus, still teaching in the temple courts, cried out, You know Me, and you know where I am from. I have not come of My own accord, but He who sent Me is true. You do not know Him,
but I know Him, because I am from Him and He sent Me.
So they tried to seize Him, but no one laid a hand on Him, because His hour had not yet come.
Many in the crowd, however, believed in Him and said, When the Christ comes, will He perform more signs than this man?
When the Pharisees heard the crowd whispering these things about Jesus, they and the chief priests sent officers to arrest Him.
So Jesus said, I am with you only a little while longer, and then I am going to the One who sent Me.
You will look for Me, but you will not find Me; and where I am, you cannot come.
At this, the Jews said to one another, Where does He intend to go that we will not find Him? Will He go where the Jews are dispersed among the Greeks, and teach the Greeks?
What does He mean by saying, You will look for Me, but you will not find Me, and, Where I am, you cannot come?
On the last and greatest day of the feast, Jesus stood up and called out in a loud voice, If anyone is thirsty, let him come to Me and drink.
Whoever believes in Me, as the Scripture has said: Streams of living water will flow from within him.
He was speaking about the Spirit, whom those who believed in Him were later to receive. For the Spirit had not yet been given, because Jesus had not yet been glorified.
On hearing these words, some of the people said, This is truly the Prophet.
Others declared, This is the Christ. But still others asked, How can the Christ come from Galilee?
Doesn't the Scripture say that the Christ will come from the line of David and from Bethlehem, the village where David lived?
So there was division in the crowd because of Jesus.
Some of them wanted to seize Him, but no one laid a hand on Him.
Then the officers returned to the chief priests and Pharisees, who asked them, Why didn't you bring Him in?
Never has anyone spoken like this man! the officers answered.
Have you also been deceived? replied the Pharisees.
Have any of the rulers or Pharisees believed in Him?
But this crowd that does not know the law, they are under a curse.
Nicodemus, who had gone to Jesus earlier and who himself was one of them, asked,
Does our law convict a man without first hearing from him to determine what he has done?
Aren't you also from Galilee? they replied. Look into it, and you will see that no prophet comes out of Galilee.
Then each went to his own home.
